goal: Find out which of INSTALL.md's claims hold in real clients beyond Claude Code, so nobody installing agent-kit in Codex or Cursor is misled, and record what was run and seen per tool (R1).
changed: docs/INSTALL.md: a dated Tested installs table (Codex CLI 0.172.0, Codex CLI 0.39.0, Cursor CLI 2026.11.22, and not verified rows for the rest), and a column in the top table saying which rows were exercised.

docs/INSTALL.md fixes: Codex needs a CLI with `codex plugin` (0.39.0 has none), `codex plugin add` installs and enables each plugin, uninstall is `codex plugin remove`; the by-hand url MCP entry needs a newer Codex; Cursor's marketplace add is per account and has no CLI install, `--plugin-dir` loads from a clone, with a context7 already in ~/.cursor/mcp.json the plugin's server can't be told apart, and Cursor also lists Claude Code's plugin skills.
HUMAN_TASKS.md H4 has exact steps for the Cursor app, the Codex app, Copilot in VS Code, pi and OpenCode; ROADMAP.md R1 has its status.

claims.claim: Codex CLI 0.172.0 installs all 7 agent-kit plugins from the published GitHub repo, and all 44 skills reach the model's prompt.
claims.check: Scratch HOME and CODEX_HOME, no credentials: codex plugin marketplace add lyddonb/agent-kit, codex plugin add for each plugin, codex plugin list (7 installed, enabled), codex debug prompt-input (44 <plugin>:<skill> entries, matching the repo's skill folders).
claims.remaining: No model turn ran a skill, and the Codex app and IDE extension were not tried.

claims.claim: In Codex CLI 0.172.0, research-tools' context7 MCP server connects.
claims.check: codex app-server over stdio, initialize then mcpServerStatus/list: context7 with pluginId research-tools@agent-kit, serverInfo Context7 4.9.1, tools resolve-library-id and query-docs.
claims.remaining: No tool call was made through a model turn.

claims.claim: Codex CLI 0.39.0 can't follow INSTALL.md: it has no plugin command and rejects a url MCP server.
claims.check: codex plugin marketplace add exits 2 (unexpected argument 'marketplace'); codex mcp list with the by-hand url entry fails (missing field `command`).
claims.remaining: Whether 0.39.0 loads skills at all wasn't run; its binary has no SKILL.md string, which suggests it doesn't (inferred).

claims.claim: Cursor CLI 2026.11.22 loads all 44 agent-kit skills from a clone of the published repo.
claims.check: One signed-in cursor-agent -p --mode ask prompt with --plugin-dir for each of the 7 plugins in a fresh clone; the 44 skill paths inside the clone match the repo's skill folders exactly.
claims.remaining: This is a local plugin load, not a marketplace install: the CLI has no install command, so the app install is in HUMAN_TASKS H4.

claims.claim: In Cursor, research-tools' context7 MCP server connects.
claims.check: Same prompt: a server named context7 connected, but the user's ~/.cursor/mcp.json already defines context7 and no server appeared under the plugin's name, so the two can't be told apart; in a scratch home, --plugin-dir with mcp list listed no servers; the resolve-library-id call was refused in -p mode.
claims.remaining: Needs a run without the user's own context7 entry, or the app check in HUMAN_TASKS H4 step 1.

claims.claim: The Codex app and IDE, the Cursor app, Copilot in VS Code, pi and OpenCode install agent-kit as INSTALL.md says.
claims.check: Not run: pi and OpenCode are not installed on the test machine, and the apps need Beau.

next.item: Beau runs the remaining install checks and fills in their rows.
next.why_now: Those rows still claim support that nobody has run, and Copilot and the Cursor app are the most likely clients for someone new.
next.impact: Anyone installing outside Claude Code and the Codex CLI gets steps that someone has actually run.

next.item: Update the Codex CLI on the test machine: Homebrew's codex formula and the npm copy are both 0.39.0, and the cask has 0.172.0.
next.why_now: On that machine, any agentfiles or agent-kit check that uses `codex` hits the 0.39.0 failures above.
next.impact: Codex picks up agent-kit's plugins there, and agentfiles' Codex checks run against a version that has plugins.

release.note: INSTALL.md now says which clients were tested and how, gives Codex CLI and Cursor CLI steps that were run, and marks the untested clients as not verified.
